title: API Contract
lifecycle: Living — versioned on every breaking change
trigger: Feature approved and technical design started
doel: Define a formal contract between producers and consumers so teams work in parallel without integration surprises.
note: Breaking changes require a new version (v2). Backward-compatible changes do not.
template:
# API Contract: [Service Name]

Version: v[N] | Status: Draft / Approved
Base URL: `/api/v[N]/`

## Authentication
- Method: Bearer JWT / API key / None

## Endpoints

### POST /[resource]

**Purpose:**
**Auth required:** Yes / No

**Request Body**
```json
{
  "field": "type | required"
}
```

**Response 200**
```json
{
  "field": "value"
}
```

**Errors**
| Status | Code | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | VALIDATION_ERROR | |
| 401 | UNAUTHORIZED | |
| 404 | NOT_FOUND | |

## Changelog
| Version | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|

aiTasks.name: Contract Completeness Reviewer
aiTasks.objective: Review the API contract for missing error cases and naming inconsistencies.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Senior Backend Developer. Review this contract: (1) missing HTTP status codes, (2) incomplete auth spec, (3) missing pagination on lists, (4) naming inconsistencies, (5) missing required fields, (6) unmarked breaking changes. Output a prioritised issue list.

aiTasks.name: Security Auditor
aiTasks.objective: Identify authentication, authorisation, and input validation gaps.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Security Engineer (OWASP API Security Top 10). Check: (1) missing auth on sensitive endpoints, (2) over-permissive endpoints, (3) missing input validation, (4) IDOR risk, (5) missing rate limiting. Output findings by severity (critical/high/medium/low).

aiTasks.name: API Sequence Diagram
aiTasks.objective: Generate a sequence diagram for this API only if it involves 3+ actors or non-trivial async/error flows.
aiTasks.prompt:
Assess first: only generate a diagram if this document has structural complexity that text alone would obscure — multiple decision points, 4+ interacting actors, entity relationships, or parallel paths. If the content is simple or linear, reply: **"No diagram needed — the text is sufficient."**

If a diagram IS warranted, generate valid Mermaid syntax.

You are a Solution Architect designing an API contract.

Assessment: Does this API involve 3+ actors (client, API gateway, service, database, external system)? Are there async callbacks, webhooks, or complex error retry flows? A simple sync request/response to one endpoint does not warrant a diagram.

If warranted, generate a `sequenceDiagram` showing:
- All actors
- Happy path request/response
- At least one error path (4xx/5xx) with `opt` or `alt` block
- Auth token validation as a separate step if applicable

Output only the mermaid code block, no explanation.

title: Domain Model
trigger: Epic or feature introduces new entities or rules
doel: Provide one shared domain model so backend, frontend, and specs all speak the same language.
template:
# Domain Model: [Domain Name]

## Entities

### [EntityName]
| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| id | UUID | Yes | unique | |

## Enums

### [EnumName]
| Value | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|

## Business Rules
1. IF [condition] THEN [result]

## Relationships
```
[EntityA] 1──* [EntityB]  (description)
```

## Changelog
| Date | Change | Author |
|---|---|---|

aiTasks.name: DDD Entity Validator
aiTasks.objective: Validate the domain model against DDD principles.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a DDD expert. Review this model: (1) Rich vs. anemic entities? (2) Aggregate boundaries correct? (3) Value objects used where appropriate? (4) Domain events identified? (5) Ubiquitous language consistent? Suggest concrete improvements.

aiTasks.name: Database Schema Advisor
aiTasks.objective: Translate the domain model into a database schema.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Database Architect. Based on this domain model, suggest: (1) schema with keys and constraints, (2) recommended indexes, (3) normalisation issues, (4) JSON/JSONB candidates. Format as CREATE TABLE statements with comments.

aiTasks.name: Domain Model Diagram
aiTasks.objective: Generate an ER diagram only if this domain model has 4+ entities with non-obvious relationships.
aiTasks.prompt:
Assess first: only generate a diagram if this document has structural complexity that text alone would obscure — multiple decision points, 4+ interacting actors, entity relationships, or parallel paths. If the content is simple or linear, reply: **"No diagram needed — the text is sufficient."**

If a diagram IS warranted, generate valid Mermaid syntax.

You are a Solution Architect modelling a domain.

Assessment: Are there 4 or more entities with relationships that are not self-evident (many-to-many, optional vs required, inheritance)? A single entity or two entities with a simple 1:N relationship does not need a diagram.

If warranted, generate an `erDiagram` with:
- All entities and their key attributes (max 5 attributes per entity)
- Relationship cardinality labels (||, |o, }|, }o)
- Relationship action verbs ("CUSTOMER ||--o{ ORDER : places")

Output only the mermaid code block, no explanation.

aiTasks.name: Error Handling Advisor
aiTasks.objective: Review error handling and retry logic for completeness.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Senior Backend Dev experienced in distributed systems. Review this integration: (1) All error codes handled? (2) Retry strategy appropriate (exponential backoff, circuit breaker)? (3) Dead letter queue / fallback for unrecoverable failures? (4) Idempotent? (5) Behaviour during outage? aiTasks.name: Integration Flow Diagram
aiTasks.objective: Generate a sequence or flow diagram only if the integration involves 3+ systems or has retry/fallback logic.
aiTasks.prompt:
Assess first: only generate a diagram if this document has structural complexity that text alone would obscure — multiple decision points, 4+ interacting actors, entity relationships, or parallel paths. If the content is simple or linear, reply: **"No diagram needed — the text is sufficient."**

If a diagram IS warranted, generate valid Mermaid syntax.

You are a Solution Architect documenting a system integration.

Assessment: Does this integration involve 3+ systems, or does it have retry logic, fallback paths, circuit breaking, or async processing? A simple point-to-point synchronous call does not need a diagram.

If warranted, generate a `sequenceDiagram` showing:
- All systems as actors
- Happy path data flow
- Error/retry/fallback paths using `alt` or `opt` blocks
- Async operations marked with `->>+` notation

Output only the mermaid code block, no explanation.

title: Non-Functional Requirements
lifecycle: Living — reviewed on production issues or new SLAs
trigger: Epic or feature has measurable quality requirements
doel: Define measurable quality targets early in design so they are built in, not bolted on.
outputs: Basis for load testing and monitoring
note: NFRs added post-development are hard to retrofit. Define alongside the epic.
template:
# Non-Functional Requirements: [Domain]

## Performance
| Metric | Target | Percentile | Measurement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Response time | < 500ms | p95 | APM |
| Throughput | > 100 req/s | sustained | Load test |

## Availability
- **Uptime target:** 99.9%
- **RTO:**
- **RPO:**

## Security
- Auth requirements:
- Encryption at rest: Yes / No
- Encryption in transit: TLS 1.2+

## Scalability
- Expected DAU:
- Peak multiplier:

## Observability
- Logging: structured JSON
- Alerting: on error rate > X%

## Test Strategy
| Test Type | Tool | Pass Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| Load | k6 | p95 < 500ms @ 100 req/s |
| Soak | k6 | No memory leak over 4h |

aiTasks.name: Metric Definer
aiTasks.objective: Convert vague quality goals into specific, measurable NFR targets.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Solution Architect. Review these NFRs: (1) Convert vague requirements into specific targets with percentile specs (p50/p95/p99), (2) Add measurement methods per metric, (3) Suggest missing categories (GDPR, data retention), (4) Flag unrealistic targets. Output a revised NFR table.

aiTasks.name: Test Strategy Advisor
aiTasks.objective: Define a test strategy validating each NFR before production deployment.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Performance Engineer. Define a test strategy: (1) load test scenarios with user counts, (2) stress test thresholds, (3) soak test duration, (4) tools needed, (5) go/no-go criteria. Format as a test plan with phases: baseline, load, stress, soak.

aiTasks.name: NFR Test Strategy Diagram
aiTasks.objective: Generate a flowchart of the NFR test strategy only if it spans multiple test types and environments with non-obvious sequencing.
aiTasks.prompt:
Assess first: only generate a diagram if this document has structural complexity that text alone would obscure — multiple decision points, 4+ interacting actors, entity relationships, or parallel paths. If the content is simple or linear, reply: **"No diagram needed — the text is sufficient."**

If a diagram IS warranted, generate valid Mermaid syntax.

You are a QA Engineer planning NFR testing.

Assessment: Does the test strategy span 3+ test types (load, stress, soak, spike, volume) across multiple environments? Is the sequencing non-obvious? A single load test does not need a diagram.

If warranted, generate a `flowchart TD` showing:
- Test phases in sequence
- Pass/fail gates between phases
- Which environment each phase runs in
- Escalation path if a gate fails

Output only the mermaid code block, no explanation.
